title: census leak_problems scans the new_rows fields
goal: census.leak_problems also scans the string fields of each new_rows entry (url, title, publisher, licence, version_or_date, used_in), naming the field and the kinds but never the value, so a tenant id or email planted in a new source row fails apply and not only the sync gate.

sys.path.insert(0,"_tools")
import census
leak="tenant "+"-".join(["7f3c2a10","5b6d","4e8f","9a1b","2c3d4e5f6a7b"])
r=census.leak_problems({"outcomes":[],"gaps":[],"conflicts":[],"new_rows":[{"url":"https://x.example.com/a","title":leak}]})

gates.question: How does leak_problems scan a new row's url, which kbpublic.file_hits strips before scanning?
options: url scanned as file_hits scans it plus an email address anywhere in the raw url
url scanned as file_hits scans it only
url scanned in full with every leak shape including guid
gates.recommendation: url scanned as file_hits scans it plus an email address anywhere in the raw url
gates.reason: because 19 existing source urls hold a guid legitimately and a full scan would refuse them
gates.answer: url scanned as file_hits scans it plus an email address anywhere in the raw url

notes: Found by the SP-ovwzbc7u review on 2026-10-23: leak_problems builds its fields from outcome notes, gap texts and conflict texts only, while new_rows go to the tracked _sources.csv through kbid.add_source, which has no leak check, so a planted GUID in a new_rows title returns no problem. The other leak_problems of ql_deliver.py and ql_store.py are separate functions and stay. Sprint SP-mk6ikval started 2026-10-26; item moved from draft to todo.
